- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods (high sentiment > 0.5) and underestimate in bearish (sentiment < 0.3), especially near recent highs.
- Overshoot after sharp price spikes; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% if sentiment drops sharply post-spike.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; apply mean reversion bias: if 3-day moving average of forecast > true, adjust down by 1–2% per day.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag in downward trends; delay downward corrections by 2–3 days if sentiment is weak.
- When sentiment is consistently low (<0.3) over 3+ days, reduce forecast slope downward by 10–15% to avoid underestimating bearish drift.
- Avoid over-optimism in early forecast days (e.g., day 1–5); cap initial forecast values at 10% below recent 7-day high if sentiment is neutral or bearish.
